commands.command:
if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
echo "name=${{ inputs.artifact_name }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "run_id=${{ inputs.artifact_run_id }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "commit_sha=${{ inputs.commit_sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
echo "name=velocity-validated-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "run_id=${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "commit_sha=${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install google-api-python-client google-auth google-auth-httplib2 google-auth-oauthlib

chmod +x distribution_scripts/*.sh
if [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/gsc-service-account.json" ] && [ -n "${GSC_SITE_URL:-}" ]; then
./distribution_scripts/deploy_distribution.sh --artifact-dir .build --key "${INDEXNOW_KEY:-}" --creds "$RUNNER_TEMP/gsc-service-account.json" --gsc-site "$GSC_SITE_URL"
else
./distribution_scripts/deploy_distribution.sh --artifact-dir .build --key "${INDEXNOW_KEY:-}"
fi

npm run atlas:build
npm run queries:join-release

npm run validate:occupancy-probe
npm run validate:occupancy-controls
npm run validate:release

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
git add -- $file_pattern
if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "no changes to commit"; exit 0; fi
git commit -m "citation occupancy probe: measured winnability -> atlas"
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
git fetch origin main
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
git rebase --abort || true
git reset --hard origin/main
npm run atlas:build
npm run queries:join-release
npm run validate:occupancy-probe
npm run validate:occupancy-controls
npm run validate:release
git add -- $file_pattern
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
echo "no changes to commit after re-deriving onto origin/main"
exit 0
fi
git commit -m "citation occupancy probe: measured winnability -> atlas"
else
npm run validate:occupancy-probe
npm run validate:occupancy-controls
npm run validate:release
git add -- $file_pattern
git commit --amend --no-edit
fi
if git push origin HEAD:main; then exit 0; fi
sleep $((attempt * 15))
done
exit 1

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
git add -- $file_pattern
if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0; fi
echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
git commit -m "query evidence refresh: measured GSC demand -> atlas -> release candidates"
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
git fetch origin main
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
git rebase --abort || true
git reset --hard origin/main
test -z "${GSC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" || python3 scripts/queries/ingest_gsc_evidence.py
npm run atlas:build
npm run queries:join-release
node scripts/selfheal/run_lane_selfheal.mjs
npm run validate:release
git add -- $file_pattern
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
exit 0
fi
git commit -m "query evidence refresh: measured GSC demand -> atlas -> release candidates"
else
npm run validate:release
git add -- $file_pattern
git commit --amend --no-edit
fi
if git push origin HEAD:main; then exit 0; fi
sleep $((attempt * 15))
done
exit 1

COUNT=$(node -e 'try{console.log((require("./data/queries/measured_demand_candidates.json").candidates||[]).length)}catch{console.log(0)}')
# The second reason to wake the release lane: routes that were admitted
# for build and never built.
#
# This step used to dispatch only when the measured atlas produced a
# candidate. That is the only lane it knew about, and the atlas has
# produced nothing for weeks - so the release lane was not running, so
# the 136-route unbuilt backlog could not have drained even after
# build_page_release_queue.js was taught to offer it. Wiring a consumer
# to a lane that never wakes is not a drain.
#
# The backlog is drainable when it holds AWAITING_RELEASE_LANE entries.
# Nothing about the ceiling changes: the lane still publishes at most
# the governed 2 new URLs a day, and a run with nothing to do exits on
# its own named stop.
BACKLOG=$(node -e 'try{console.log((require("./data/content/unbuilt_rich_page_backlog.json").routes||[]).filter(r=>String(r.disposition||"").toUpperCase()==="AWAITING_RELEASE_LANE").length)}catch{console.log(0)}')
# The third reason, and the one that makes a landed artifact safe: an
# agent run that is still waiting to be absorbed.
#
# Velocity Content Release triggers on the push that ADDS a manifest.
# That is one attempt. On 2026-09-02 the TRT run landed at 13:51, the
# lane ran at 13:52 on that exact sha and died at validate:release on
# the recovery-store midnight defect; absorption and publish never ran,
# the manifest stayed READY_FOR_ABSORPTION and trt/index.html was
# untouched. Nothing retried, because a retry needs a NEW manifest and
# that manifest had already landed. The defect was fixed and merged
# three hours later and the artifact was still stranded: the fix had
# nothing to run on.
#
# A schedule on the release lane itself is not available - this repo
# permits exactly one scheduled committer and workflow-runtime-mutations
# enforces it - so the catch-up belongs here, in the lane that already
# holds that permission and already dispatches for two other reasons.
# The release lane's absorption step re-walks every manifest on disk, so
# a dispatch IS the retry; nothing else has to change.
PENDING=$(node scripts/citation_velocity/count_unabsorbed_agent_runs.mjs)
if [ "$COUNT" -gt 0 ] || [ "$BACKLOG" -gt 0 ] || [ "$PENDING" -gt 0 ]; then
echo "measured demand produced $COUNT candidate(s); $BACKLOG route(s) await the release lane in the unbuilt backlog; $PENDING landed agent run(s) are still unabsorbed; dispatching Velocity Content Release"
gh workflow run velocity-content-release.yml --ref main
else
REASON=$(node -e 'try{console.log(require("./data/queries/measured_demand_candidates.json").stop_reason||"unstated")}catch{console.log("candidates file unreadable")}')
echo "no candidates this run, the unbuilt backlog is empty, and every landed agent run is absorbed; not dispatching. Named stop: $REASON"
fi

npm run cadence:gate
npm run cadence:template-share

if [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" != "main" ]; then
echo "REFUSED: this lane pushes HEAD:main; refusing to run on $GITHUB_REF_NAME" >&2
exit 1
fi

git fetch origin main
git checkout main
git reset --hard origin/main

set -euo pipefail
if [ -n "${VELOCITY_RELEASE_TARGET:-}" ]; then
echo "operator supplied batch_size=$VELOCITY_RELEASE_TARGET; leaving the budget capped as requested"
echo "VELOCITY_RELEASE_MAX=$(( VELOCITY_RELEASE_TARGET > 150 ? VELOCITY_RELEASE_TARGET : 150 ))" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
exit 0
fi
BUDGET="$(node scripts/citation_velocity/resolve_release_budget.mjs)"
echo "VELOCITY_RELEASE_TARGET=$BUDGET" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
echo "VELOCITY_RELEASE_MAX=$(( BUDGET > 150 ? BUDGET : 150 ))" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
echo "resolved processing budget: $BUDGET row(s)"

python3 scripts/queries/ingest_gsc_evidence.py
npm run atlas:build
npm run queries:join-release

npm run citation:prepare-velocity-intake
npm run build:cached
npm run selfheal:release
npm run validate:release

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
git add -A
if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0; fi
echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
git commit -m "absorb agent runs $(date -u +%F)"
# The base this absorption was built and validated against. If a rebase
# moves it, the rebased tree has to be re-derived and re-validated
# before it may be pushed to main.
BASE_BEFORE_REBASE="$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)"
# The retry loop used to be unreachable. `git rebase` is a bare command
# under `bash -e`, so a conflicting rebase killed the step on attempt 1
# and attempts 2 and 3 never ran - 2026-08-27 died on
# "could not apply ... absorb agent runs" with no retry and no sleep.
#
# Every file that conflicts here is derived: artifacts/validation/*.json
# and content/_shared/content_state.json are outputs of the intake and
# build below, not hand-authored state. Merging two generated versions of
# a generated file is meaningless, so a conflict is resolved by taking
# the newest main and re-deriving the absorption on top of it. That keeps
# whatever the concurrent push added, which `reset --hard` before the
# re-derive guarantees and a plain "ours" resolution would have dropped.
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
git fetch origin main
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
git rebase --abort || true
git reset --hard origin/main
npm run citation:prepare-velocity-intake
npm run build:cached
npm run selfheal:release
npm run validate:release
git add -A
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
exit 0
fi
git commit -m "absorb agent runs $(date -u +%F)"
elif [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)" != "$BASE_BEFORE_REBASE" ]; then
# A CLEAN rebase still produces a tree nobody validated.
#
# This step validated the absorption against the main it started
# from, then rebased onto whatever main had become, then pushed.
# A rebase that applies without conflict is not a rebase that
# changes nothing: origin/main moved - that is why we are rebasing -
# so the tree being pushed is a combination of two validated trees,
# which is not itself a validated tree. The push surface here is
# main.
#
# Both sibling push loops in this repo already close this: the
# Velocity step below, and velocity-full-rebuild.yml, each re-run
# build + validate:release after a successful rebase and amend the
# result. This step was the only one that did not, and it is the
# step that runs first and most often.
#
# Only re-derive when the base actually moved. A rebase onto the
# same base is a no-op and re-validating it would double the
# runtime of every clean run for nothing. build:cached makes
# this specific case - re-deriving after nothing this lane
# changed - a near-instant restore instead of a full rebuild.
npm run build:cached
npm run selfheal:release
npm run validate:release
git add -A
git commit --amend --no-edit
fi
if git push origin HEAD:main; then exit 0; fi
BASE_BEFORE_REBASE="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"
sleep $((attempt * 15))
done
exit 1

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
git add -A
if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0; fi
echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
git commit -m "velocity content release $(date -u +%F)"

# Same unreachable-retry defect as the absorption step: a bare `git rebase`
# under `bash -e` ended the step on the first conflict. Aborting a failed
# rebase leaves a clean tree so the remaining attempts can actually run.
# This loop does not re-derive on conflict the way the absorption step
# does, because the commit it is replaying carries published pages from
# release:velocity-intake that a reset would discard and this step cannot
# regenerate on its own.
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
git fetch origin main
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
git rebase --abort || true
sleep $((attempt * 15))
continue
fi
npm run build:cached:prune
# The cadence ledger records what the sitemap held the last time the gate
# ran. cadence_gate.js writes it, but the only other job that runs the gate
# is Validate Repo, which is read-only - so its copy dies with the runner.
# Nothing ever committed the ledger, so it stayed frozen at whatever a human
# last pushed (2026-08-27). Every page published after that read as "new",
# and the moment more than new_pages_per_week accumulated, the gate blocked
# Validate Repo permanently: the comparison it depends on could never
# advance on its own. Running it here - inside the loop that already
# rebuilds and amends - is what makes the ledger persist. It also enforces
# the weekly cap at the point of publication, where refusing is still
# possible, rather than after the pages are already on main.
npm run cadence:gate
# This step follows release:velocity-intake, which can publish new
# pages via release:velocity-content. `npm run build` restores
# data/release/frozen_page_registry.json for a newly-accepted route
# but does not derive every store a publish can move - a raw
# validate:release here HARD_FAILed on a healthy publish three
# separate times on 2026-09-03: accepted-artifact-recovery (run
# 33725560369, no recover:accepted-artifacts run), then the
# historic-page-maximum ratchet and historic-artifact-recovery when
# five repaired pages legitimately grew past their recorded ceiling,
# then agent-fix-ledger-truthfulness (run 33785501356) when the same
# publish made 17 baselined claims newly true. Every one of those has
# a registered repair_command; this is the one push surface in the
# repo whose entire job is publishing content, so - unlike
# query-evidence-refresh.yml, which deliberately stays self-heal-free
# for exactly this reason - there is no boundary against a build-shaped
# repair here. Routing the check through self-heal instead of a raw
# validate:release closes the whole class at once: any current or
# future release-profile validator with a registered repair gets
# repaired before it can block the push, rather than each one being
# found and patched by hand as the next lane failure.
npm run selfheal:release
# Then prove it UNHEALED. self-heal exits 0 when its own re-validation is
# clean, but that re-validation is the one it just repaired into being
# clean; a raw release-profile pass on the healed tree is a separate,
# unassisted statement that the tree about to reach main is green. It also
# keeps workflow-data-trace's "a release revalidation precedes every push"
# satisfied by code rather than by the word validate:release appearing in
# a comment, which is how this step satisfied it before.
npm run validate:release
npm run trace:agent-exact
npm run validate:agent-exact
npm run trace:citation-agent-fixes
npm run validate:citation-agent-fixes
git add -A
git commit --amend --no-edit
if git push origin HEAD:main; then exit 0; fi
sleep $((attempt * 15))
done
exit 1

if [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" != "main" ]; then
echo "REFUSED: this lane pushes HEAD:main; refusing to run on $GITHUB_REF_NAME" >&2
exit 1
fi

git fetch origin main
git checkout main
git reset --hard origin/main

npm run intelligence:build
npm run release:full-rebuild

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
git add -A
if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0; fi
echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
git commit -m "velocity full rebuild $(date -u +%F)"

# The retry loop was unreachable. `git rebase` is a bare command under
# `bash -e`, so the first conflicting rebase ended the step and attempts
# 2 and 3 never ran - the same defect fixed in velocity-content-release.yml
# on 2026-08-28, still present here because this workflow has never run
# once and so nothing ever exercised it. It is the recovery workflow, which
# makes an unreachable retry the worst place for this to sit.
#
# Aborting a failed rebase leaves a clean tree so the remaining attempts
# can actually run. It deliberately does not re-derive the way the
# absorption step does: the commit being replayed is a full deterministic
# rebuild, and this workflow's declared failure boundary forbids broad
# self-healing here.
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
git fetch origin main
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
git rebase --abort || true
sleep $((attempt * 15))
continue
fi
npm run build:cached:prune
npm run validate:release
git add -A
git commit --amend --no-edit
if git push origin HEAD:main; then exit 0; fi
sleep $((attempt * 15))
done
exit 1
